{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement (Customer Side)

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel
**Re:** Playbook review of the Master Services Agreement (Copperleaf / Vendor)
**Status:** 19 findings reviewed — 2 critical, 7 high, 8 medium, 1 low, 1 requiring manual confirmation

---

## 1. Executive summary

The Agreement as drafted is not signable in its current form. Two critical issues and a cluster of high-severity commitments transfer nearly all risk to us:

- **No Vendor indemnity at all.** Section 20 is a one-way, unlimited Customer indemnity covering "every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services," with no IP infringement, data-breach, law-violation or wilful-misconduct coverage and no claim-handling procedure. Section 9.3 cross-refers to infringement remedies "required by Section 20.5," which does not exist — confirming the omission.
- **The liability cap is illusory.** One month of Fees actually paid, "without exception," against a USD 2,000,000 annual take-or-pay commitment. The "without exception" language overrides the Excluded Claims definition in Section 21.3, pulling indemnification, confidentiality, data protection, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement inside a one-month cap.
- **A three-year, USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay commitment** "without reduction or termination rights" (Section 2.1) drives three separate findings (minimum commitment, liquidated damages, termination for convenience). Exposure of up to USD 6,000,000 survives even our Section 9.4 convenience termination and Section 27.3 force-majeure termination.
- **Restrictive covenants bind only us:** full-term exclusivity (Section 2.2) and a worldwide, 24-month post-term non-compete (Section 12.4).
- **Internal inconsistency is pervasive and works against us.** Section 12.3 expressly states that Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment — flatly contradicting Sections 2.1, 2.2 and 12.4. Section 13.1 (revocable, Customer-only licence) contradicts Sections 13.2–13.3. Section 11.1 (immediate deletion, no assistance) contradicts Sections 11.2–11.3 and 10.1.

On the positive side, assignment and change of control (Section 24), audit rights (Section 22), governing law and venue (Section 28), auto-renewal and uplift caps (Sections 8.2–8.3), MFN (none burdening us) and Vendor insurance (Section 18) already meet or exceed our preferred positions and require no redline.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | § 20 (Customer-only indemnity; dangling ref to § 20.5) |
| 2 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | Deviation | § 21.1 (one month of Fees, "without exception") |
| 3 | High | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Deviation | § 2.1 (3-year USD 2M/yr take-or-pay) |
| 4 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties payable by Customer | Deviation | § 2.1 (take-or-pay as functional liquidated amount) |
| 5 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 2.1 (conflicts with § 9.4 convenience right) |
| 6 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 2.2 (Vendor as sole and exclusive provider) |
| 7 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 (worldwide, 24 months post-term) |
| 8 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 13.1 (revocable at Vendor's discretion; Customer alone) |
| 9 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 (with §§ 24.2–24.4, 13.3) |
| 10 | Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination assistance and data return | Deviation | § 11.1 (immediate cessation and deletion) |
| 11 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 19.2 (15-day warranty; remedy cut-off) |
| 12 | Medium | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 14.2 ("upon creation" vs. "subject to payment") |
| 13 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22.1 (with §§ 22.2–22.3) |
| 14 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28.1 (with §§ 28.2–28.3) |
| 15 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | Compliant | § 8.2 (with § 8.3) |
| 16 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Compliant | § 12.3 (with §§ 7.1, 8.3) |
| 17 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Needs review (verification failed) | § 12.3 |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1 (with § 18.2) |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following are at or beyond our playbook walk-away thresholds and should be treated as conditions of signature:

1. **§ 20 — No Vendor indemnity (critical).** A one-way, unlimited Customer indemnity with no Vendor IP, data-breach or law-violation coverage is the playbook walk-away position. We require a Vendor indemnity (IP, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Security Incident or Customer Data disclosure, injury, gross negligence and wilful misconduct), a standard notice/control/cooperation procedure, customary IP exclusions, and procure-modify-replace-refund remedies at § 20.5 (which also cures the dangling § 9.3 cross-reference). Our indemnity narrows to Customer-provided content and our breach of law. No super-cap fallback is needed because indemnity obligations are already Excluded Claims under § 21.3.
2. **§ 21.1 — One-month liability cap (critical).** Below our six-month walk-away floor and illusory against the § 2.1 commitment; "Fees" (§ 1.5) also excludes implementation charges. We require the greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, with the § 21.3 Excluded Claims restored as uncapped. §§ 21.2–21.3 otherwise meet the playbook and are untouched.
3. **§ 2.1 — Three-year USD 2M/yr take-or-pay (high).** Walk-away on minimum commitment and above the liquidated-damages threshold; it also guts our § 9.4 convenience right and contradicts §§ 7.1 and 12.3. Preferred: delete, with Fees owed only for Services ordered and actually used. Fallbacks: a 12-month commitment reducible on 30 days' notice with a true-up, and/or an early-termination fee capped at three months' Fees as the sole liquidated amount. At minimum, termination and reduction rights must be carved out so § 9.4 remains effective and the commitment reduces pro rata.
4. **§ 2.2 — Vendor as sole and exclusive provider (high).** Full-term exclusive dealing with no category limit, time limit or performance exit is the walk-away position, and it conflicts with § 12.3. Preferred: delete. Fallback if commercially necessary: 12 months, category-limited, terminable on SLA failure.
5. **§ 12.4 — 24-month worldwide non-compete (high).** Exceeds the walk-away threshold (post-term duration over 12 months and undefined "competes with Vendor" scope) and contradicts § 12.3. Preferred: delete. Fallback: named product, term only, ≤12 months, with carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions.
6. **§ 13.1 — Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion, Customer only (high).** Close to walk-away and inconsistent with §§ 13.2–13.3. We extend the grant to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, make it transferable per § 13.3, and limit revocation or suspension to the § 13.3 notice-and-cure standard, leaving §§ 13.2–13.4 undisturbed.
7. **§ 11.1 — Immediate cessation of assistance and permanent deletion (medium severity, walk-away substance).** Squarely our walk-away position and contradicts §§ 11.2, 11.3 and 10.1. We require up to six months of transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates, with deletion subordinated to §§ 11.2–11.3. Fallback: 90 days.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the seven walk-away items above, plus the two remaining substantive deviations: § 19.2 (extend the Deliverable/software warranty to 12 months and services to 90 days, and delete the post-period cut-off so the § 19.4 remedy and § 19.5 non-exclusivity survive) and § 14.2 (Deliverable title vests on creation; remove the payment condition, with a fallback conditioning vesting only on payment of undisputed Fees for the specific Deliverable — Vendor keeps its § 13.3 suspension remedy).
2. **Lead the negotiation with § 12.3.** Vendor's own acknowledgement that we have made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment is our strongest lever against §§ 2.1, 2.2 and 12.4; ask Vendor to confirm which provision it intends to govern.
3. **Flag the drafting defects** for Vendor to correct: the missing § 20.5 referenced in § 9.3, the duplicate paragraph numbering at § 2.2, and § 23 (Records and Customer Assurance), which is a heading with no substantive text.
4. **Resolve the NOSOLICIT finding (§ 12.3) before sign-off.** Verification failed on this item, so we should not rely on it. Counsel to re-run the review for any non-solicitation, no-hire or personnel-restriction covenant and confirm the position manually before we close the issues list.
5. **Confirm no redline is needed** on the compliant items — §§ 24 (assignment and change of control), 22 (audit), 28 (governing law and venue), 8.2–8.3 (renewal and uplift cap), 12.3/7.1/8.3 (no MFN burdening us) and 18 (insurance) — and protect them from erosion in later turns.
6. **Escalate commercially** if Vendor refuses the § 20 indemnity, the § 21.1 cap, or the § 2.1 commitment: these three together determine whether the deal is signable.

*This memo reflects only the verified findings supplied and the playbook positions cited in them. No other legal conclusions are drawn.*"}
